question: What is the code name of India’s first successful Nuclear test?
solution:
​The correct answer is __**Smiling Buddha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The code name of India’s first successful Nuclear test was **Smiling Buddha**.
 
• India on **May 18, 1974**,** **conducted its first nuclear test, codenamed **'Smiling Buddha'**, in Rajasthan's **Pokhran**, becoming a nuclear power.
 
• The bomb was detonated on the army base Pokhran Test Range, in Rajasthan,** by the Indian Army** under the supervision of several key Indian generals.
 
• At the time of Indian Prime minister **Indira Gandhi**. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) characterized this test as a **"peaceful nuclear explosion"**.
 
• In May **1998**, India again conducted a series of nuclear tests at the **same location**, it was called **Pokhran-2** tests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Code Name**
 **Description**
 
 

 Laughing Buddha
 The Laughing Buddha is a symbol of happiness, contentment, and prosperity. but **Smiling Buddha** was the assigned code name of India's first successful nuclear bomb test on 18 May 1974.
 
 

 Operation Shakti
 
 
In May 1998, India again conducted a series of nuclear tests at the **Pokhran, **in Rajasthan, it was called **Operation Shakti**.

 
These tests are also called **Shakti–98, Shakti-I, Shakti-V, and Pokhran-2.**

 
 
 

 Operation Vijay
 
 
**Operation Vijay (1961**) was the operation by the Military of India that led to the capture of Goa, Daman, and Diu, and the Anjediva Islands.

 
**Operation Vijay (1999)**, which was the name of the Indian military operation to clear out the Kargil sector.
